exec: Mobile money fraud in Burkina Faso caused losses of "plus de 104 millions de FCFA" in October, per the Ministry of Security.
geo_basis: country as the source states it
plain: Burkina Faso's Ministry of Security says mobile money scams hit 263 people in October and cost "plus de 104 millions de FCFA", within 956 cybercrime victims that month.

key_findings: The Ministry of Security, on its broadcast Réflexe sécurité, reported that mobile money diversions affected 263 people, with losses of "plus de 104 millions de FCFA" in October 2026.
956 people were victims of cybercrime in October 2026.
Total financial loss from cybercrime in October 2026 estimated at "plus de 261 millions de FCFA" (Lefaso.net, source line DCRP/MSECU).
report.publisher: Burkina Faso Ministry of Security (as relayed by beninwebtv.com)
recommendations: Check the seller's identity before any transfer; share no confidential code; keep exchanges and payment proof; report via Alerte-BCLCC or by phone to the brigade.

summary: Burkina Faso's Ministry of Security, on its broadcast Réflexe sécurité, made public October 2026 cybercrime figures, according to Benin Web TV and Lefaso.net. It says 956 people were victims of cybercrime in October, with losses of "plus de 261 millions de FCFA" per Lefaso.net, and that mobile money scams affected 263 people and caused losses of "plus de 104 millions de FCFA". The ministry's release itself was not read.
title: Burkina Faso ministry: mobile money scams cost "plus de 104 millions de FCFA" in October

validation.note: Two independent publishers, Benin Web TV and Lefaso.net (source line DCRP/MSECU), each relay the Ministry of Security figures; the ministry's own release was not read.

review.note: wording: source calls Réflexe sécurité an émission (broadcast), not a programme; fixed in summary and key finding. Date, 263 people, plus de 104 millions de FCFA, 956 victims, ministry attribution and BCLCC advice match the Benin Web TV article.
